text:
jdoe-cust: Hey team — after our Okta SSO migration, several users at AcmeCorp (org_id: org_1234) are getting 403 when they try to view Compliance > Audit. They used to see logs fine. Error in UI: \"access_denied: missing entitlement audit_logs:read\". This is blocking an audit next week. Any ideas?

sam-support: Thanks — can you share repro steps and an example user? Are they org admins in Redwood or a different role? Also, did you change SCIM/group provisioning recently?

jdoe-cust: They're marked as Admin in our Redwood org. We provisioned via SCIM and updated group names in Okta during the migration. Quick repro:

curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token-of-affected-user>\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/org_1234/audit/logs\"

Response: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"access_denied","message":"missing entitlement: audit_logs:read"}

maria: Can you paste an anonymized decoded ID token or access token claims for one affected user? We need to confirm whether the entitlement claim is present. If you can't share the whole token, just the claim names and values. Also confirm whether your Okta mapping sends \"entitlements\" or group names in a custom claim.

jdoe-cust: Here's a redacted ID token payload for one affected user (removed sub/jti):

```json
{
  \"iss\": \"https://dev-xxxx.okta.com\",
  \"aud\": [\"api.redwood.ai\"],
  \"exp\": 1977004834,
  \"iat\": 1977001234,
  \"email\": \"alice@acme.com\",
  \"groups\": [\"Okta:SecurityAdmin\"],
  \"roles\": [\"admin\"]
  // NOTE: no \"entitlements\" claim
}
```

eng-identity: Looks like the token has groups but not the entitlement claims our authorization layer checks for. Background: for audit/compliance access we require either the user to have an org-level Admin role (backed by our DB) OR the token must include an \"entitlements\" claim containing \"audit_logs:read\" (or a mapped equivalent). In SCIM-first setups we prefer to provision entitlements as part of the user object (SCIM attribute \"entitlements\").

In Okta you can either:
1) Add an OIDC claim mapping that emits \"entitlements\" from group membership, e.g. a Custom Claim with Expression: `Array.map(user.groups, g => g.indexOf(\"SecurityAdmin\") >= 0 ? \"audit_logs:read\" : null).filter(Boolean)` (pseudocode)
2) Or ensure SCIM provisioning includes `entitlements` on the user resource when you push to Redwood.

To validate quickly: decode the token and look for \"entitlements\" or call our tokeninfo endpoint:

```bash
curl -X POST https://auth.redwood.ai/introspect -d 'token=<access_token>' -H 'Authorization: Basic <client_creds>'
```

It will return JSON with claims we see. If \"entitlements\" is missing, that's the cause.

sam-support: Temporary workaround — we can grant the affected users the `audit_logs:read` entitlement from the Console under Org Settings > Entitlements for org_1234. That will restore access while you update Okta mappings. If you want, we can script it with the admin API: 

```bash
POST /v1/orgs/org_1234/entitlements
Auth: Bearer <org-admin-token>
Body: { \"user_id\": \"<redacted>\", \"entitlement\": \"audit_logs:read\" }
```

deploy-bot: Ticket #45678 created and escalated to eng-identity oncall. Priority: P1 (audit compliance).

oncall-ops: I'm taking this — will check SCIM sync logs and Okta claim mappings. ETA ~4h. Can you share the timestamp range for when you last ran a full SCIM sync? Also, did you change group names (e.g., SecurityAdmin -> SecAdmin) during the migration?

jdoe-cust: We ran a full SCIM sync last night. We did rename one group from \"SecurityAdmin\" to \"SecAdmin\" but also kept an alias mapping in Okta. SCIM logs show successful updates but we didn't include entitlements field anywhere.

oncall-ops: Found it — SCIM user PATCHes did not include the entitlements attribute. The Okta custom profile for \"entitlements\" wasn't mapped to the Okta group expression. We'll push a fix to include entitlements on the SCIM user resource and trigger a re-provision. After that affected users will need to get a new token (re-login) or we can revoke their session to force a refresh.

eng-identity: Also worth noting: audit log retention settings are gated by a separate entitlement: \"compliance:view_retention\". If someone has `audit_logs:read` but not the retention entitlement they can see logs but not the retention policy page. We should surface clearer error messages for both. I'll file a follow-up to improve message text to indicate which entitlement is missing.

jdoe-cust: Thanks — can you apply the temporary Console entitlement for 3 users now while you push the SCIM fix? Also please confirm when the tokens will be refreshed.

sam-support: Yep — we can apply the entitlement now. I've queued the change and will confirm once done. For token refresh: if you prefer we can revoke sessions via Admin Console which forces reissue immediately; otherwise waiting for normal token expiry (~1h).

deploy-bot: Entitlement change applied for users: alice@acme.com, bob@acme.com, carol@acme.com. Ticket updated.

oncall-ops: SCIM mapping fix deployed to staging; schedule deploying to prod at 02:00 UTC after narrow maintenance window. We'll post here when done and confirm tokens are emitting entitlements.

jdoe-cust: Appreciate the fast turnaround. Please keep me posted — this was critical for our audit.

maria: following up — improvement ticket created to add a clearer API error body that returns the missing entitlement name(s) in the 403. Also tracking doc updates for common Okta mapping recipes.

jdoe-cust: Thanks all :thumbsup:
